companion_paper.title: Functional Network-Based Analysis of Industrial Robot Dynamics
companion_paper.locator: §3.1, §3.2 and Table 1 (test geometry, motion and 500 Hz internal logging); §3.3 (numerically derived velocity), Figure 9 (signal definitions).
companion_paper.finding: The five-axis industrial robot has a motor-side and a secondary arm-side encoder. Its A1 first base joint executes controlled angular steps. The paper describes a broader motion and TCP experiment plan than the public ZIP.

coverage.signals: Reference and actual current, reference and actual position, processed velocity. The backlash trial alone explicitly separates motor and arm-side encoder positions.
coverage.preprocessing: Counted every archive CSV; SHA-256 collapsed identical V35 baseline data before any fit. All six first-row velocity cells are missing. Time and both current channels are finite and strictly increasing time was checked.
coverage.fit: Fit actual current to intercept + slope × reference current, pooling the four other byte-distinct runs. All samples of the held run were unseen. Different run lengths weight training by sample count. One-step sample index alignment; no lag search.

evidence: Five separate-run fits have slopes 0.73768–0.73862, signed correlation 0.99900–0.99996. Across leave-one-run-out tests the zero-intercept/unit-gain error spans 0.2390–0.3836 versus affine error 0.00119–0.02040 RMSE in stored current units.

The backlash trace reaches a 0.022534-degree difference between motor and arm displacements, after subtracting both initial positions. This observed difference includes transmission dynamics, encoder effects and compliance.
bounds: No calibrated current-limit event flag, power-stage limit, independently sensed motor torque, or joint controller gain schedule appears in the released CSVs. A near-constant current scaling or the largest observed error does not identify clipping.

The held-out groups are five disclosed traces, not five machines or unseen TCP placements. The archive filenames all use P16. Current column units/gain conventions are not specified by their CSV headers.
reproduction: Python 3.12.14, NumPy 2.3.5, SciPy 1.17.0. Run scripts with their directory on the Python path. CSVs are deterministic summaries of the credited source files.
Download data.zip from the recorded Zenodo file URL, verify size and publisher MD5, then run python derive_axis.py data.zip OUTPUT.
